## Task: fix nested-class serialization in Django migrations (TASK.md)

**The bug.** When a field kwarg holds a class defined inside another class — e.g. `EnumField(enum=Thing.State)` where `State` is an inner `enum.Enum` — `TypeSerializer.serialize()` built the reference from `__name__` instead of `__qualname__`, producing `repro.models.State` (wrong: `State` lives at `repro.models.Thing.State`). The generated migration then fails at import/migrate time. (Ground: my step-16 `makemigrations` run showing `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'repro.models.Outer'; 'repro.models' is not a package` — the nested-path import failure that motivated the fix.)

**The fix** — one line, `django/db/migrations/serializer.py:272` (`TypeSerializer.serialize`):

```diff
-                return "%s.%s" % (module, self.value.__name__), {"import %s" % module}
+                return "%s.%s" % (module, self.value.__qualname__), {"import %s" % module}
```

This matches Django's own upstream fix for the same ticket family (`29d8198841` "Fixed #27914 -- Fixed serialization of nested classes in migrations", present on `origin/main` as `qualname(self.value)` — verified by reading `origin/main:django/db/migrations/serializer.py`).
